Subject: Control plane probe & sampling questions for our on‑prem pilot

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the review call this morning. We have two quick asks before we sign the connectivity runbook:

1) We need a short description of probe points you intend to place inside the on‑prem control plane (ingress LB, control API node, and agent egress). For our SOC audit we must show where telemetry is collected and what is sampled vs. full‑capture.

2) Proposed sampling rates and retention for trace/log/flow artifacts (we have limited on‑prem storage). Stedi's security team expects a defensible sampling rationale tied to incident triage SLOs.

I've attached a rough topology. If you can provide a one‑page checklist we can include in the vendor attestation pack, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Alice

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Control plane probe & sampling questions for our on‑prem pilot

Alice —

Thanks — good questions. Summary answers inline, and attaching a short probe diagram + sampling matrix for your SOC pack.

Quick summary:
- Probe locations: control API node (read‑only tap of request/response headers), ingress/load‑balancer fronting control plane (flow logs + connection metadata), and egress gateway agent (selected full‑capture for errors). We also recommend a host‑level heartbeat metric exported to your Prometheus pull endpoint.
- Sampling rationale: default 1:1000 flow sampling for high‑volume control plane telemetry, 1:100 for API header captures tied to authenticated calls, and 100% capture for any traffic flagged with error response codes or auth failures. Retention proposal: 30 days aggregated metrics, 7 days traces (samples), 90 days for compressed flow indexes required by audit.

Action items we propose for the runbook:
1) Include a short attestation table with probe URIs and stored artifact types.
2) Add a trigger rule: if error rate > 0.5% over 5m window, escalate to 100% short‑window capture for 1 hour.
3) Provide a stubbed example of redaction rules for PII in headers (we'll hand off the template).

Sending attachments now. If you want, Jon or Irene can join your SOC call on Thursday to walk the auditors through the probe diagram.

—Rachel
Product Security & Deployments
Redwood Inference

Rachel / team —

Quick status:
- Control API tap: implemented as a passive proxy on port 8443 (read‑only, TLS terminator disabled for the tap). CPU impact measured at ~0.7% p50 on our staging box at 500rps; estimate 1.5% p50 at 2k rps. Endpoint path: /internal/ctl‑tap/v1/streams/{probe_id}. We will publish example curl and ACLs in the runbook snippet.
- LB sampling: tested with sFlow proxy — collector accepts 1:1000 without backpressure at 10Gbps. We'll include NetFlow fallback in the doc.
- Error trigger: implemented as a short pipeline rule in the collector; on error conditions (5xx or auth fail) we flip a flag to stream full headers + body for 1 hour. We also persist an index entry that keeps a compressed fingerprint for 365 days (auditable).

Marissa — draft attached: "probe‑attestation‑table.csv" (also copied into the shared drive link). I left the retention column conservative per Stedi's ask; happy to tune.

Next steps: I'll join Alice's SOC call on Thu if you want me there. Otherwise we can send the one‑page PDF and the runbook snippet.

—Irene
